classification.difficultyReason: Select the taught square-sum obstruction without an immediate hence scaffold, compute the sum from coefficients, and interpret its negative sign as contradicting four real roots.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $x^4+2x^3+4x^2-x+5=0$ cannot have four real roots.

answer.short: The sum of the squares of the roots is $(-2)^2-2(4)=-4<0$, which is impossible if all four roots are real.
answer.worked:
Let the roots be $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta$.
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta&=-2\\\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\alpha\delta+\beta\gamma+\beta\delta+\gamma\delta&=4\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2&=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta)^2\\&\quad-2(\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\alpha\delta+\beta\gamma+\beta\delta+\gamma\delta)\\&=(-2)^2-2(4)\\&=-4<0\end{aligned}$$
If all four roots were real, each square would be non-negative, so their sum would be non-negative. Therefore the equation cannot have four real roots.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that $3x^4-6x^3+7x^2+2x-8=0$ cannot have four real roots.

answer.short: The sum of the squares of the roots is $2^2-2\left(\dfrac73\right)=-\dfrac23<0$, which is impossible if all four roots are real.
answer.worked:
Let the roots be $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta$.
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta&=-\frac{-6}{3}=2\\\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\alpha\delta+\beta\gamma+\beta\delta+\gamma\delta&=\frac73\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2&=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta)^2\\&\quad-2(\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\alpha\delta+\beta\gamma+\beta\delta+\gamma\delta)\\&=2^2-2\left(\frac73\right)\\&=-\frac23<0\end{aligned}$$
If all four roots were real, each square would be non-negative, so their sum would be non-negative. Therefore the equation cannot have four real roots.
